An '''officer's disk''' (or '''disc'''), was an insignia and coding device used in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|military branch]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="BTM" /> since its early [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. They were already worn in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] by the graduates of the first Imperial class from the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|military academies]].<ref name="DVGP1">[[Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison 1|''Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison'' 1]]</ref> Such disks contained coded identification information<ref name="BTM" /> and consisted of a metallic stepped cone shape appearing to be three disks stacked on top of one another. Code disks were featured on the hat and belt buckle<ref name="SWVD" /> of the most high-ranking [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]]. Their function was similar to that of the [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]], which were also part of the officers' [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|service uniform]].<ref name="BTM" />

When the Galactic Empire collapsed following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="ROJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the code disks remained in use within the Imperial splinter factions, along with the rest of the Imperial uniform.<ref name="HEC" />

==Behind the scenes==
In an interview published in the [[Star Wars Insider 98|ninety-eighth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', [[Wikipedia:Costume designer|costume designer]] [[John Mollo]] revealed the "officers' disks" came from a shop in [[Wikipedia:Borehamwood|Borehamwood]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]], where the [[Elstree Studios]] are located. They were in fact spare pulleys from the middle of a record player, and Mollo's costuming crew actually ordered about five hundred of them.<ref name="Insider98">{{InsiderCite|98|Fabric of the Universe}}</ref>
